name: Defect-Hitting Criterion for Convex Learning-Space Restrictions
statement: For a finite partial cube $G$, a vertex $r$, and a convex subgraph $C$ containing $r$, the vertex $r$ is a valid root of $C$ exactly when $C$ contains no complete fork of an $r$-defect of $G$. Consequently $C$ is a learning-space graph exactly when it contains a $C$-antipodal pair $r,\bar r$ and every $r$-defect fork loses a vertex outside $C$. For a semicube, every retained defect centered inside must use the boundary $\Theta$-class.
proof: Orient every coordinate away from $r$. A failure of closedness is exactly a pair of outgoing incident edges without their square. Convexity ensures that any parent square whose fork remains in $C$ also remains entirely in $C$. A valid root supplies an opposite state by taking the union of states containing every active coordinate after translating the root to empty.
